newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Two French aid workers in Afghanistan to be tried.
newsitem.headline: Two French aid workers in Afghanistan to be tried.

text.p: Two French aid workers arrested by Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban last month are to be tried on Wednesday, the Foreign Ministry in Kabul said.
"The two Frenchmen are scheduled to be tried tomorrow at the governors office in the 10th precinct," said a note from the ministry delivered on Tuesday.

The two men, Frederic Michel and Jose Daniel Llorente, were arrested with five of their local staff on February 21. They were working in Kabul for the Paris-based charity Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger) at the time.
They were arrested after a farewell lunch hosted by the charity's female expatriate staff for some 70 of their local women workers.

Although the charges against the two men have not been officially released, officials have said that they have been investigated for what the Taleban consider "immoral deeds", including being in the same compound as unveiled Afghan women.
Taleban fighters raided the lunch, arresting two male local staff, and seized cameras, photographs, video cassettes and magazines.

The three other local men were arrested at the residence later in the day. The two Frenchmen were taken from a United Nations compound where they were staying at 2 a.m. the following morning after prolonged negotiations between U.N. and Taleban officials. The U.N. Security Council has protested the incursion into U.N. premises and demanded the release of the two expatriate workers.
The two men have been held in a converted office in a prison in central Kabul since their arrest. They have been allowed frequent visits from other expatriates and supplies of food and cigarettes.

The head of the U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan Norbert Holl visited Kabul on March 11 to discuss the case with senior Taleban officials. He told reporters afterwards he believed that the case would be dealt with quickly and leniently.

"I was not given a date for their release, but I was promised that they would deal with this in the near future, and I have the feeling they will do it in the spirit of clemency." said Holl at the time.
A foreign offical closely involved with the case told Reuters recently that the Taleban leadership had four main concerns.

"They need to placate their hardliners, and they need to satisfy their moderates. They also want to demonstrate that they have followed the due process of law, and to show that Islamic Law is a merciful regime," the official, who asked not to be named, said on Monday.
He also pointed out that the period of the Islamic New Year, which falls on Thursday, is a traditional time of amnesty.
